root.name: Latvian Gambit: Corkscrew Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5 3. Nxe5 Nf6 4. Bc4 fxe4 5. Nf7 Qe7 6. Nxh8 d5

overview: In the Corkscrew Gambit White grabs the rook on h8 with the knight, while Black gets the knight trapped and develops with tempo. Black has given the exchange and more for the trapped knight and quick development. White can try to extract the knight with Bxd5 while Black attacks with ...Qh4 and ...c6.

white_ideas.idea: Free the h8 knight with Nf7 ideas or Bxd5
Return material to neutralise the attack

black_ideas.idea: Win the trapped knight with ...Qh4 or ...Bg4
Use the open lines for the attack

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with a White knight stuck on h8

character.notes: Wild tactical play with trapped pieces and mates.

gambit.notes: Black gave the rook and can regain the knight.

approach.notes: The Latvian is an anchor for offbeat.

character.reason: Trapped pieces and open lines make play forcing.

gambit.reason: Black has given the exchange for a trapped knight and development.

soundness.reason: The Latvian and its Corkscrew lines are considered dubious.
